brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L gap to Mars Plastics' prices and move to 30-day payment to free up ₹10.63 L cash

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics' prices on HDPE bottles and PP caps
priceAsk.target: Cut ₹16.09 L from our yearly spend — bring the 30 mL bottle down from ₹1.65 to ₹1.38 and the 28 mm cap from ₹0.90 to ₹0.81
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics already gives us those exact prices on the same items — the 30 mL bottle is 19.6% cheaper there and the cap is 11.1% lower; the market ask for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap sits at ₹0.85–0.95 typical, so our ₹0.90 is fair but Mars' ₹0.81 shows real room exists

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days after receipt

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue or cash position. Our ₹1.29 Cr yearly spend is real money to a private converter, but without their numbers we lean on what we do know: Mars already sells us identical parts for less, and we have five strong backup packaging firms lined up. That gives us the room to push hard on price and to ask for faster payment — they'll want to keep the volume.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹16.09 L every year compared to Mars Plastics
The 30 mL HDPE bottle costs us ₹1.65 here versus ₹1.38 at Mars — a 19.6% gap — and that one SKU alone costs us ₹11.74 L extra per year
The 28 mm PP cap costs ₹0.90 here and ₹0.81 at Mars, an 11.1% gap worth ₹4.23 L yearly

Market asking prices for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap run ₹0.55–1.20 per piece, typically ₹0.85–0.95, with modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — our ₹0.90 is market-fair but Mars' ₹0.81 proves tighter pricing is real
Cutting payment terms from 45 to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L of our cash
We spend ₹1.29 Cr a year with them — a meaningful piece of business for a private packaging converter

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter doing pharma bottles, caps and preforms — top second-source candidate with scale and a decent health score

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader in pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong, profitable, robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed firm with moulded and blow-moulded packaging capability across bottles and caps

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we're flying blind on their cash position and stability — watch for any supply hiccups and qualify a second source fast
Mars already beats them on price for identical parts; if we push too hard here without a backup locked in, Premier might walk and leave us scrambling

The market ask shows our current ₹0.90 cap price is fair versus the ₹0.85–0.95 typical band, so the big savings are really in matching Mars — don't expect them to go below that without a volume or spec trade
Faster payment (30 days) frees up cash for us but tightens it for them; if they're already stretched, pair the payment ask with a volume commitment or a longer contract to sweeten the deal
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep you as a supplier, but right now Mars Plastics gives us the same bottles and caps for ₹16 lakh less every year — let's talk about closing that gap and moving to 30-day terms.
